narrative:
On October 5, 2026, the Karnataka High Court listed 3,264 matters across 54 judges, hearing 1,362 cases for an overall hearing rate of 41.7%. This represents a moderate contraction compared to October 1 (46.4% across 2,832 listings) and September 29 (49.1%), though it marks an improvement over the 39.5% conversion recorded on September 30. Total scheduled caseload reached its highest volume across the observed four-day sample.

Individual judicial efficiency varied considerably across halls. Notable high performers included Justice V. Srishananda in Court Hall 23, who heard 65 of 78 scheduled matters (83.3%), and Justice K.S. Hemalekha in Court Hall 30, addressing 84 of 112 listings (75.0%). Conversely, extreme docket congestion severely depressed throughput in specific rooms. Court Hall 2A under Justice T.P. Vivekananda heard only 8 of 234 listed matters (3.4%), while Court Hall 27 under Justice S. Rachaiah (0 of 98) and the Chief Justice's Division Bench in Court Hall 1 (0 of 37) heard none of their scheduled listings.

Stage-wise conversion reflected typical procedural prioritization. Preliminary hearings converted at the highest rate among major stages at 67.6% (257 of 380 heard). The core volume rested in orders (41.9% of 1,085 heard) and admission matters (43.7% of 830 heard). Final hearings continued to exhibit a clearance bottleneck, converting just 22.7% (154 of 679 heard), a sharp drop from the 35.8% conversion rate seen on October 1. By case category, Writ Petitions (WP) formed the largest segment with 1,361 scheduled cases, maintaining a stable 48.0% hearing rate. In contrast, Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) experienced a major slowdown, converting only 23.0% (119 of 518 heard), down substantially from the ~49% rates registered on September 29 and October 1.
